decisions.reason: As a core rye bread close to the firm's established competence, it likely meets minimum aspiration levels and does not yet justify problemistic search away from it.
The repeat gold medal is a clear above-aspiration signal versus comparable products, so management would be very unlikely to withdraw it.
A seeded rye mixed bread fits current bakery demand and existing production routines, so with no negative signal the firm would give it more time.
Its darker malted rye profile is somewhat more niche and overlaps with other rye breads, raising review risk, but not enough to force withdrawal after only one year.
A marzipan stollen still fits the seasonal Christmas range and can be carried with modest slack, though it lacks the strong quality signal seen for the raisin premium stollen.
The ancient-grain bread matches a premium natural positioning and, as a very recent launch, would usually be retained while management learns whether results settle above aspiration.
